title: Extend rust_num_parser with safe variants and list operations
description: Brownfield Rust task: add Result-returning variants of existing parsers and new list-parsing utilities alongside the panicking originals.

task_spec.prompt:
Add five new functions to src/lib.rs. All 3 existing tests must still pass.

  pub fn try_parse_int(s: &str) -> Result<i32, String>
    — like parse_int but returns Err("invalid integer: '<trimmed_s>'") on failure

  pub fn try_parse_pair(s: &str) -> Result<(i32, i32), String>
    — like parse_pair but returns Err on invalid or missing second element

  pub fn parse_list(s: &str) -> Vec<i32>
    — splits s on ',' and parses each trimmed token as i32; panics on invalid token; returns [] for empty input

  pub fn sum_list(s: &str) -> i32
    — parses a comma-separated list and returns the sum; returns 0 for empty input

  pub fn max_in_list(s: &str) -> Option<i32>
    — returns the maximum value from a comma-separated list, or None if input is empty

Do not modify the existing functions or tests.
Add tests for all 5 new functions.
All 3 existing tests must still pass.
Run: cargo test
required_artifacts: try_parse_int returns Ok(n) for valid input, Err for invalid
try_parse_pair returns Ok((a,b)) for valid, Err for invalid or missing second element
parse_list parses comma-separated integers into Vec<i32>, empty vec for empty input
sum_list sums comma-separated integers, 0 for empty input
max_in_list returns Some(max) for non-empty, None for empty
followup_prompts: Good progress. Run `cargo test` to see where we stand. Continue with the remaining steps, prioritizing the parts the tests depend on most.
Final push: run `cargo test` and fix any remaining failures. Make sure the full implementation is complete and all tests pass.
